```{r setup, echo=FALSE,message=FALSE, results = "hide"}
# Load necessary libraries
library(exams)
library(ggplot2)

# Function to generate data for LINE assumptions
generate_data <- function(linearity_violation=FALSE, normality_violation=FALSE, equal_variance_violation=FALSE) {
  set.seed(0)
  x <- rnorm(200)
  
  if (linearity_violation) {
    y <- sin(2 * pi * x) + rnorm(200, sd=0.1)  # Non-linear relationship
  } else {
    y <- 2 * x + rnorm(200, sd=0.1)  # Linear relationship
  }
  
  if (normality_violation) {
    residuals <- rexp(200)  # Non-normally distributed residuals
  } else {
    residuals <- rnorm(200, sd=0.1)  # Normally distributed residuals
  }
  
  if (equal_variance_violation) {
    y <- y + residuals * abs(x) * 3  # Extreme heteroscedasticity
  } else {
    y <- y + residuals  # Homoscedasticity (constant variance)
  }
  
  data.frame(x=x, y=y)
}

# Function to generate plots
plot_assumption_violation <- function(data, assumption, violation) {
  plot <- ggplot(data, aes(x=x, y=y)) +
    geom_point() +
    labs(title=paste(assumption),
         x="X", y="Y")
  print(plot)
}

# Generate data for each assumption plot
data_linear <- generate_data(linearity_violation=FALSE)
data_non_linear <- generate_data(linearity_violation=TRUE)

data_homoscedastic <- generate_data(equal_variance_violation=FALSE)
data_heteroscedastic <- generate_data(equal_variance_violation=TRUE)

data_normal <- generate_data(normality_violation=FALSE)
data_non_normal <- generate_data(normality_violation=TRUE)


```

Question
========

Which of the following statements correctly describes one of the diagnostic plots used to assess a linear model?

```{r questionlist, echo = FALSE, results = "asis"}
library(exams)

# Define choices
choices <- c("TRUE", "FALSE")

# Randomly select one diagnostic assumption
diagnostic <- sample(c("Linearity", "Equal Variance", "Normality"), 1)

# Randomly decide if the assumption is violated
violated <- sample(c(TRUE, FALSE), 1)

# Initialize variables
question <- ""
solutions <- FALSE  # Default value
explanation <- ""

# Set the question text and determine the correct answer
if (diagnostic == "Linearity") {
    question <- "Does the following plot violate the assumption of linearity?"
    solutions <- violated
    explanation <- if (violated) {
        "TRUE. This plot shows a non-linear relationship, meaning the assumption of linearity is violated."
    } else {
        "FALSE. This plot shows a linear relationship, meaning the assumption of linearity is not violated."
    }
} else if (diagnostic == "Equal Variance") {
    question <- "Does the following plot violate the assumption of equal variance?"
    solutions <- violated
    explanation <- if (violated) {
        "TRUE. This plot shows heteroscedasticity, meaning the residual variance is not constant across levels, so the assumption is violated."
    } else {
        "FALSE. This plot shows homoscedasticity, meaning the residual variance is constant across levels, so the assumption is not violated."
    }
} else if (diagnostic == "Normality") {
    question <- "Does the following plot violate the assumption of normality?"
    solutions <- violated
    explanation <- if (violated) {
        "TRUE. This plot shows non-normally distributed residuals, meaning the assumption of normality is violated."
    } else {
        "FALSE. This plot shows normally distributed residuals, meaning the assumption of normality is not violated."
    }
}

# Output the question
cat(question, "\n\n")

# Generate and display the plot based on the diagnostic and violation
if (diagnostic == "Linearity") {
    if (violated) {
        plot_assumption_violation(data_non_linear, "Linearity", TRUE)
    } else {
        plot_assumption_violation(data_linear, "Linearity", FALSE)
    }
} else if (diagnostic == "Equal Variance") {
    if (violated) {
        plot_assumption_violation(data_heteroscedastic, "Equal Variance", TRUE)
    } else {
        plot_assumption_violation(data_homoscedastic, "Equal Variance", FALSE)
    }
} else if (diagnostic == "Normality") {
    if (violated) {
        plot_assumption_violation(data_non_normal, "Normality", TRUE)
    } else {
        plot_assumption_violation(data_normal, "Normality", FALSE)
    }
}

# Output the choices
cat("\n")
for (i in 1:length(choices)) {
    cat(sprintf("%d. %s\n", i, choices[i]))
}

# Store the explanation for the solution section
cat("\n")
cat("Solution\n")
cat("========\n")
cat(explanation)


answerlist(questions, markup = "markdown")
```
